```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h1.csv")

h2Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1

Respondents with doctoral or equivalent professional degrees will have lower relationship satisfaction in their relationships.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

\- **Degree Group (**\`**degreeGroup**\`**):** A categorical variable with two groups: doctoral/professional and other education. Other education describes any level of education reported below a doctoral/professional degree.

\- **Relationship Satisfaction (**\`**relSat**\`**):** A composite variable including the average scores of each participant in a relationship's responses to 7 point Likert-type scales asking for their relationship satisfaction, contentment, and happiness: \`prqc_1\`, \`prqc_2\`, \`prqc_3\`.

This dataset only includes respondents who were dating, in a commited relationship, or married.

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$degreeGroup)

# Summarize relationship satisfaction  separately for each group. 
by(h1Data$relSat, h1Data$degreeGroup, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig-satisfaction shows the distribution of average relationship satisfaction by degree group. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarizes the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-satisfaction
#| fig-cap: "Average relationship satisfaction by degree group."
#| fig-width: 8 
#| fig-height: 5 

h1Viol <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x= degreeGroup,
                     y= relSat,
                     fill= degreeGroup))+
  geom_violin()+
  geom_boxplot(width=.12)+
  labs(x="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       y="Mean relationship satisfaction score",
       fill="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       title="Relationship Satisfaction by Level of Education")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Viol
```

## H2. Male time spent grooming hair and time spent on social media.

Male respondents who spend a lot of time grooming their hair daily will also report a lot of time spent on social media daily.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

\- \*\*Daily time spent grooming hair (Time_A_hair_1):\*\* a single variable of each male respondents time spent grooming their hair daily between 0-360 minutes.

\- \*\*Daily time spent on social media (Time_social_media_1):\*\* a single variable of each male respondents time spent on social media daily between 0-360 minutes.

This data set only includes respondents who answered "male" when asked for their sex at birth.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("Time_A_hair_1", "Time_social_media_1")])
```

### Graph

@fig-time shows the relationship between male respondents' time spent grooming their hair daily and time spent on social media daily. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-time
#| fig-cap: "Daily time spent grooming hair and daily time spent on social media."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5 

nrow(h2Data)
nrow(unique(h2Data[,c("Time_A_hair_1","Time_social_media_1")]))

h2Jitter <- ggplot(
  data=h2Data,
  aes(x= Time_A_hair_1,
      y= Time_social_media_1))+
  geom_jitter(width = .12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size = .6)+
  labs(x= "Time spent grooming hair daily (minutes)",
       y= "Time spent on social media daily (minutes)",
       title= "Minutes Spent Grooming Hair Daily and Minutes Spent on Social Media Daily")+
  theme_gray(base_size = 18)

h2Line <- h2Jitter + geom_smooth(method="lm")

h2Line
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, h2Data$Time_social_media_1, use = "complete.obs")
round(r,2)
```

The correlation was 0.25, indicating a weak positive association. Male respondents who reported more time spent on grooming their hair daily reported more time spent on social media daily.
